findings.evidence: Diff lines 174-178: `ext m` / `-- The center-linear structure on ModuleCat acts through the inclusion of the center.` / `rfl`. `extClass_center_smul` at Scalar.lean:182 is stated with `Module.End.smulLeft`, not with the Linear scalar action, so every consumer has to bridge the two.
findings.fix: State a named lemma for discrete modules (e.g. `center_smul_id_eq_homMk_smulLeft`), prove it with the linear-structure simp lemmas, and use it in place of `hz`.
findings.issue: `hz : z • 𝟙 M = ObjectProperty.homMk (ModuleCat.ofHom (Module.End.smulLeft (z : A) z.property))` is closed by `ext m; rfl`. This relies on the wrappers `Linear.fullSubcategory`, `ModuleCat.Algebra.instLinear` and `Subalgebra.centerAlgebra` unfolding to the same thing. The comment says what happens but not why `rfl` holds. The fact is reusable: it links the center's scalar action to `extClass_center_smul` (Scalar.lean:182), which later R5.2 steps will need again.

findings.evidence: Diff: `have hf ... := Submodule.liftQ_apply _ _ _` inside the definition body and `outerExtClass_mk ... := (rfl)` below it.
findings.fix: Make the base-ring `liftQ` map a private definition. Build `outerExtClass` from it with `{ f with map_smul' := … }`, moving the scaling proof into a separate private lemma. Then `outerExtClass_mk` and `hf` can both use `Submodule.liftQ_apply` again.
findings.issue: `outerExtClass_mk` changed from `Submodule.liftQ_apply _ _ _` to `(rfl)`. It now holds only because the tactic-built definition (`let f`, `refine {…}`, `liftQ`) unfolds. The local `hf` inside the definition restates the same computation rule.

summary: The center-linear upgrade rests on an undocumented `rfl` across several wrapper instances (`hz`) and turns the computation rule into a `(rfl)` that only holds because the tactic-built definition unfolds. Factor both into explicit lemmas.
